paragraphs.title: No One Can Stand Against the Leviathan or God

easy.explanation: Job 41:9 says, “Behold, the hope of him is in vain.”
easy.q: What happens to a person’s hope when facing the Leviathan?

easy.explanation: The verse asks, “Who then is able to stand before me?”
easy.q: Who is able to stand before God?

easy.explanation: Job 41:11 says, “whatsoever is under the whole heaven is mine.”
easy.q: To whom does everything under heaven belong?

answers: The Leviathan’s power and the inability to stand against him
medium.explanation: The passage first describes the creature’s terrifying strength and then declares God’s sovereignty over everything under heaven.
medium.q: What leads from the description of the Leviathan to the comparison with God?

medium.explanation: The phrase means that the person’s hope will fail.
medium.q: What does “in vain” mean in “the hope of him is in vain”?

answers: No one can place God under obligation by giving to Him first
medium.explanation: The verse emphasizes that no one has given God something first in a way that obligates Him to repay.
medium.q: What conclusion follows from “Who hath prevented me, that I should repay him?”

answers: As equal to him in strength
As unable to stand against him
challenge.explanation: The creature’s appearance and power make human hope futile and inspire fear.
challenge.q: How is a human being portrayed before the Leviathan?

answers: Both emphasize that humans lack power and ownership before God
Both describe the weakness of the sea
challenge.explanation: The first stresses that no one can stand before God, while the second stresses His ownership of all things.
challenge.q: What connection exists between “Who then is able to stand before me?” and “whatsoever is under the whole heaven is mine”?

answers: From the Leviathan’s terror to God’s supremacy and ownership of all
challenge.explanation: The passage moves from the creature’s overwhelming power to God’s claim over everything under heaven.
challenge.q: What is the main movement of thought in these verses?

short_answers.question: According to Job 41:9, what is in vain?
short_answers.answer: The hope of the person who faces the Leviathan.
short_answers.explanation: The verse says, “Behold, the hope of him is in vain.”

short_answers.question: Who is able to stand before God?
short_answers.explanation: Job 41:10 asks, “who then is able to stand before me?”

short_answers.question: What belongs to God?
short_answers.answer: Whatever is under the whole heaven.
short_answers.explanation: Job 41:11 says, “whatsoever is under the whole heaven is mine.”

easy.explanation: The passage describes his scales as his pride, shut together as with a close seal.

answers: His face, mouth, teeth, and scales
easy.explanation: The verses focus on his garment, bridle, face, mouth, teeth, and scales.
easy.q: What is described in this section?

easy.explanation: The verses say, “One is so near to another” and “They are joined one to another.”

answers: It forms a closed, impenetrable covering
It keeps him from opening his mouth
medium.explanation: The scales are shut together and cannot be separated, forming a strong covering.
medium.q: How does the joining of the scales affect the Leviathan’s protection?

medium.explanation: Here, scales are the hard protective coverings on the creature’s body.
medium.q: What does “scales” mean in this passage?

answers: His teeth are terrible all around his mouth
medium.explanation: Job 41:14 says, “his teeth are terrible round about.”
medium.q: Why does the description of the mouth and teeth increase the sense of danger?

answers: The scales are joined and cannot be separated
challenge.explanation: The text says, “They are joined one to another... that they cannot be sundered.”
challenge.q: Which detail shows that the armor is not merely made of separate pieces?

answers: The Leviathan appears protected and dangerous
challenge.explanation: His scales protect him, while his mouth and teeth inspire terror.
challenge.q: What effect comes from combining the description of the armor with the description of the teeth?

challenge.explanation: The scales create powerful protection, and the mouth and teeth create a threatening image.
challenge.q: What quality is shared by the description of the scales and the mouth?

paragraphs.title: Fire, Smoke, and Power in the Body

easy.explanation: Job 41:20 says, “Out of his nostrils goeth smoke.”
easy.q: What comes from the Leviathan’s nostrils?

easy.explanation: The passage describes burning lamps and sparks of fire coming from his mouth.
Job 41:24 says, “His heart is as firm as a stone.”

answers: They present him as a glowing and powerful creature
They show that he is weak
medium.explanation: His sneezing gives light, his eyes shine, and fire and smoke come from him.
medium.q: How do light, fire, and smoke contribute to the description of the Leviathan?

answers: Fear and sorrow retreat before him
He gives light to the sea
medium.explanation: The phrase portrays sorrow as unable to remain before his strength.
medium.q: What does “sorrow is turned into joy before him” suggest?

medium.explanation: A heart firm as stone represents courage and stability.
medium.q: What does the description of his firm heart teach about him?

answers: His eyes shine, fire comes from his mouth, and smoke comes from his nostrils
Stones come from his nostrils, and smoke comes from his eyes
Water comes from his mouth, and darkness comes from his eyes
challenge.explanation: This sequence follows the descriptions in Job 41:18–21.
challenge.q: Which sequence correctly describes the sources of light, fire, and smoke?

answers: Both strengthen the image of the Leviathan as impossible to frighten
Both show that he is weak
challenge.explanation: His firm flesh and heart emphasize strength and fearlessness.
challenge.q: What connection exists between a solid body and a firm heart in the description?

answers: The Leviathan appears unusually powerful and terrifying
challenge.explanation: Light, fire, and smoke together create an extraordinary and frightening image.
challenge.q: What impression is created by combining threatening light with smoke and flames?

easy.explanation: The passage says that swords, spears, arrows, and other weapons cannot prevail against him.
easy.q: What happens to weapons used against the Leviathan?

easy.explanation: The verses mention a sword, spear, dart, habergeon, arrows, slingstones, and other weapons.
easy.q: Which weapons are mentioned in the passage?

easy.explanation: Job 41:29 says, “he laugheth at the shaking of a spear.”
easy.q: How does the Leviathan respond to the shaking of a spear?

medium.explanation: The weapons are presented as unable to prevail against him.
medium.q: What do the sword, spear, dart, and habergeon have in common?

answers: The metals seem weak and ineffective against him
The metals make him a king
The metals sink into the sea
medium.explanation: Even strong materials are treated as worthless when used against the Leviathan.
medium.q: What does it mean that iron is counted as straw and brass as rotten wood?

answers: He remains undisturbed and laughs at the spear
medium.explanation: He does not flee, and the shaking of a spear causes him no concern.
medium.q: How is the Leviathan’s response to weapons described?

answers: Many different weapons fail against him
challenge.explanation: The passage lists many weapons and materials that cannot harm him.
challenge.q: What most strongly supports the conclusion that the Leviathan is invulnerable rather than merely stronger than one person?

answers: It shows that every kind of weapon is useless against him
It shows that only brass is strong
It shows that the Leviathan needs weapons
challenge.explanation: Iron, brass, arrows, stones, and spears all fail to trouble him.
challenge.q: What is the effect of mentioning weapons made from different materials, such as iron and brass?

answers: It presents the stones as extremely heavy
It presents them as light and powerless in his sight
It presents the Leviathan as afraid of them
challenge.explanation: Slingstones are treated as though they were merely dry straw.
challenge.q: How does calling slingstones “stubble” emphasize the Leviathan’s strength?

paragraphs.title: Turbulence in the Sea and Kingship over Creatures

easy.explanation: Job 41:31 says, “He maketh the deep to boil like a pot.”
easy.q: What does the Leviathan’s movement do to the sea?

easy.explanation: The verse says, “He maketh a path to shine after him.”
Job 41:34 says, “he is a king over all the children of pride.”
easy.q: How is the Leviathan described in relation to the children of pride?

answers: The deep boils and the sea is stirred, leaving a path
medium.explanation: His movement makes the deep boil and leaves a shining path behind him.
medium.q: What does the Leviathan’s movement cause in the water?

medium.explanation: In this context, “the deep” means the depths of the sea.
medium.q: What does “the deep” refer to in “He maketh the deep to boil like a pot”?

answers: His lack of fear supports his description as ruler over other creatures
His lack of fear shows that he is weak
medium.explanation: A creature made without fear is fittingly portrayed as a king over the proud and mighty.
medium.q: What is the connection between fearlessness and kingship?

answers: The shining path left behind him
challenge.explanation: The text specifically says that a path shines after him.
challenge.q: Which detail shows that the Leviathan’s influence continues after he has passed?

answers: No creature on earth is comparable to him
He lives only on the ground
He is weaker than every other creature
challenge.explanation: The statement emphasizes his unmatched nature on earth.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from “Upon earth there is not his like”?

answers: The boiling sea demonstrates his power, while kingship expresses his status
The boiling sea cancels his kingship
challenge.explanation: His movement transforms the sea, and his final title expresses his supremacy over other great creatures.
challenge.q: How do the description of the boiling sea and the description of kingship fit together?
